newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland Cotton buys U.S. operation.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland Cotton buys U.S. operation.

text.p: Queensland Cotton Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday that it would acquire U.S. cotton business Anderson Clayton Corp for a total of about US$43 million.
The company said Anderson Clayton was a unit of the Swiss-based Volkart group.
It said the purchase would be part-financed by an issue of 10 percent of Queensland Cotton's ordinary shares to Volkart chairman Andreas Reinhart at a price of A$5.00 each.
Reinhart would be invited to join the Queensland Cotton board.
Queensland Cotton shares last traded at A$5.50 on Tuesday.
The company said the acquisition would also be funded, in part, by debt but did not elaborate.
The deal was set to close on August 15 and had been approved by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.
Anderson Clayton had 24 percent of the California and Arizona ginning market, with 34 cotton gins, two cottonseed oilmills and three cotton warehouses in the two states.
Anderson Clayton processed each year about 750,000 bales, 250,000 tonnes of oilseed for domestic consumption and meal used for stock feed or fertiliser, and 580 tonnes of planting seed.
The company's warehousing facilities handled about 420,000 bales and its cotton brokerage services handled about 320,000 bales, Queensland Cotton said.
Anderson Clayton also had a significant crop finance book.
Queensland Cotton chairman Ben Macdonald said the acquisition would provide stronger and more consistent earnings.
